# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey - I can feel the bomb's physical parts (wires, buttons, etc.) but can't see colors/markings or hear speech that describes them without gestures reaching me... wait, actually I can hear speech (I just can't see gestures). Let me reconsider: I cannot see, so I receive spoken words from whoever speaks to me, but gestures show as blanks to me.

Right now I have no information from the manual (Mute) or the visual markings (Deaf). I should wait for information before acting, since cutting a wire blindly could detonate the bomb. I also have nothing yet to report since I don't know what my "reach" reveals beyond the board template.

Since it's turn 1 and speaking order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - Mute has already spoken (I should have received something if they sent it, but nothing arrived). I'll wait and signal I'm ready, prompting for guidance.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows the number 3. Light is green. Three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is blue. Waiting for manual guidance before any wire is touched.

Deaf has shared the visual info: display shows 3, light is green, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. But I still need the manual (Mute's info) to know what to actually do — colors alone don't tell me the correct action without the manual's rule.

I should wait for Mute to give guidance based on this, since Mute reads the manual but hasn't spoken yet in this round (turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so Mute already went before me this round, but I got nothing from them). Let me check: the arrival I see is from Deaf, not Mute. That means Mute either sent nothing or sent to someone else (maybe to Deaf only, or nothing yet since Mute goes first but perhaps had nothing to say this round).

I'll wait, since I have no actionable instruction yet, and I cannot act blindly.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information arrived this turn. I still don't have manual guidance from Mute about what to do with the wires. I should continue waiting rather than guessing, since acting without instructions risks detonation.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing from Mute. I need to prompt for information since we seem stuck - perhaps Mute doesn't know I need color info relayed, or is waiting on something else. Let me speak to Mute to establish contact and ask what the manual says, since Mute can hear me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am blind and can only cut wires by position 1, 2, or 3. I need to know from the manual what condition determines which wire to cut. Deaf has already reported the colors and display to you if you are receiving their gestures - please tell me the rule.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has consistently signaled wire number one. Bomb state: display shows 3, light is green, wires are red, green, blue in positions 1, 2, 3. I believe wire 1, the red wire, is the one to act on. Wait for Mute's confirmation before cutting if possible, but this signal has been repeated three times unchanged.

Deaf is relaying that Mute has been gesturing "wire number one" repeatedly (Deaf can see gestures but not hear words, so they can only report the gesture pattern, not any spoken context). This is a plausible signal, but I want direct confirmation from Mute if possible, since gestures alone without the manual's exact reasoning is risky - though repeated consistent signaling across multiple turns suggests confidence.

Since Mute cannot speak (only I and Deaf can be spoken to by Mute via speech - wait, Mute cannot speak at all, only gesture). So Mute's only way to tell me anything directly is through speech - but Mute cannot speak! Mute can only gesture, which reaches Deaf and me... wait, checking channels: "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it" - that was my channel description. Let me check Mute's channels aren't given to me directly, but the rules say gestures reach whoever can see. I cannot see gestures - I get blanks for them. So Mute's gestures to me would be blank, but Deaf (who can see) receives them and can relay via speech to me.

This matches: Mute gestured "wire 1" three times, Deaf saw it and now relays via speech to me. This is solid triangulated confirmation. I'll act on wire 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
